definitions.explanation: A region that receives heavy snowfall, especially the areas along the Sea of Japan coast in northern Honshū, such as Niigata, Akita, and Yamagata prefectures. Also the title of Kawabata Yasunari's famous novel.

examples.japanese: {新潟|にいがた}は{雪国|ゆきぐに}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Niigata is known as snow country.

examples.japanese: {雪国|ゆきぐに}の{暮|く}らしには{独特|どくとく}の{知恵|ちえ}がある。
examples.english: Life in snow country has its own unique wisdom.

examples.japanese: {川端|かわばた}{康成|やすなり}の『{雪国|ゆきぐに}』は、{国境|くにざかい}の{長|なが}いトンネルを{抜|ぬ}けると{雪国|ゆきぐに}であった、という{書|か}き{出|だ}しで{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: Kawabata Yasunari's Snow Country is famous for its opening line about emerging from a long tunnel at the provincial border into snow country.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{雪国|ゆきぐに} typically refers to the Sea of Japan side of northern Honshū, which receives extremely heavy snowfall due to moisture-laden winds from the sea hitting the mountain ranges. Prefectures like {新潟|にいがた}, {秋田|あきた}, {山形|やまがた}, and {富山|とやま} are representative {雪国|ゆきぐに} areas.

The word is also inseparable from {川端|かわばた}{康成|やすなり}'s 1937 novel 『{雪国|ゆきぐに}』(Snow Country), one of the most famous works of modern Japanese literature.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雪国|ゆきぐに}の{暮|く}らし (life in snow country)
- {雪国|ゆきぐに}{育|そだ}ち (raised in snow country)
- {雪国|ゆきぐに}{特有|とくゆう}の (unique to snow country)
